Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

fact noun

also the fact that, the facts, the facts speak for themselves

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.32: rem enim opīnor spectārī oportēre, nōn verba
Traupman 97: rēs ipsa indicat, the facts speak for themselves
Traupman 312

rēs, reī f.

noun, fifth declension

the fact, the facts, what really is (as against words or opinion)

Lewis & Short sets it against verba, opīniō and nōmen.

Other words

  • rē vērā — in fact, in reality, really

    phrase: ablative of rēs with vērus · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.5.1: et rē vērā; Cic. Div. 2.110 (Lewis & Short, s.v. rēs)

    Sometimes written as one word, rēvērā (Lewis & Short).

  • quod (+ indicative) — the fact that …

    conjunction · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.4.1: fēcistī mihi pergrātum, quod Serāpiōnis librum ad mē mīsistī; Traupman 97; Traupman 312

  • factum, factī n. — a deed, an act

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Ter. Eun. 5.4.19: dicta et facta (Lewis & Short, s.v. faciō)

    Not a fact in the modern sense: classically a deed or an exploit, and factum est means “it was done, it happened”.

Examples

  • rem enim opīnor spectārī oportēre, nōn verba

    for I think it is the facts that should be looked at, not the wordsCic. Tusc. 5.32

  • Piscēs illī, quī annō tōtō in memoriā ejus crēverant, rē vērā nōn minōrēs appāruērunt

    Those fish, which had grown in his memory all year, turned out in fact to be no smallercomposed

  • fēcistī mihi pergrātum, quod Serāpiōnis librum ad mē mīsistī

    it was very kind of you to send me Serapio’s bookCic. Att. 2.4.1

  • Rēs loquitur ipsa.

    The facts speak for themselves.Cic. Mil. 53 (Lewis & Short s.v. loquor)

  • Rēs ipsa indicat.

    The facts speak for themselves.Ter. Eun. 4.3.16 (Lewis & Short s.v. indicō)

See also real, true, actually.
